Wellington's Victory. Also known as the Battle of Vitoria or the Battle Symphony, Ludwig van Beethoven's Wellington's Victory, Op. 91, completed in 1813, is a highly programmatic orchestral work. It was composed to celebrate the British Duke of Wellington's victory over Napoleon's French forces at the Battle of Vitoria in Spain. The piece is notable for its literal sound effects representing battle and its usage of patriotic folk tunes to signify the opposing armies.

The battle itself occurred in 1813 in Spain, in which Arthur Wellesley defeated Joseph Bonaparte. The work specifically does not depict the Battle of Waterloo, which came later. Although regarded by music critics and even by Beethoven himself as a popular novelty rather than serious art, it was one of the most lucrative and popular successes of his lifetime.

Beethoven originally wrote the piece for the Panharmonicon, a mechanical automated orchestra invented by Johann Nepomuk Mälzel, the inventor of the metronome. He later adapted the work for live orchestra. Patriotic melodies are used to represent the nations. Rule, Britannia represents the British, while Marlborough s'en va-t-en guerre, popularly known as "For He's a Jolly Good Fellow," represents the French. The work concludes with a fugal fantasy on "God Save the King."

Special effects include literal artillery simulation, calling for percussionists to fire muskets offstage and strike large bass drums on opposite sides of the stage to represent British and French cannon fire. These sound effects give the work an unprecedented level of programmatic realism for its time. The piece premiered at the same concert as Beethoven's Seventh Symphony in Vienna in December 1813.

The financial success of Wellington's Victory was massive, outshining the public reception of the Seventh Symphony at that same premiere. Mälzel, who co-created the piece, was a close friend of Beethoven and his invention of the metronome revolutionized how tempo was mathematically measured. The work was designed as a money-maker during the inflation-plagued later years of the Napoleonic Wars, and it succeeded brilliantly in that regard.
